name: the Philippines
heroAlt: Campus of a partner medical university in the Philippines
tagline: Four NMC-aligned partner universities, an American-model MD curriculum taught entirely in English, and the hospital exposure that actually gets you through the FMGE.
intro: The Philippines has taught medicine in English for over seventy years, on a curriculum built to the American model. For an Indian student that means no language barrier, a degree recognised at home, and clinical training in genuinely busy hospitals.

why.title: English from day one, everywhere
why.text: Lectures, examinations, ward rounds and patient conversations all happen in English. There is no local-language exam to clear before you can begin, and no translation between you and a patient.

why.title: A curriculum built for the FMGE
why.text: The Philippine MD follows the American model, which maps closely onto what the FMGE and NExT actually test. This is why Philippine graduates have historically performed well in the Indian screening exam.

why.title: Hospitals with real patient volume
why.text: Our partner universities train students across affiliated hospitals running into thousands of beds. You take histories and present cases rather than watching from the back of the room.

why.title: An established Indian community
why.text: Thousands of Indian students already study across these campuses. Indian food, familiar festivals and seniors who have been through the same process are all already in place.

why.title: Four campuses, one honest recommendation
why.text: Davao, Cebu and Dagupan each suit a different student, budget and NEET profile. A LIMRA counsellor will tell you which of the four fits you, including when the answer is none of them.

clinical.intro: Across our four Philippine partners, students rotate through affiliated hospitals with several thousand beds between them, beginning patient contact in the early years rather than in the final ones.

name: Timor-Leste
heroAlt: Campus of a partner medical university in Timor-Leste
tagline: Two NMC-aligned partner universities in Dili, English-medium teaching, and a lower total cost than most routes into medicine abroad.
intro: Timor-Leste is a younger destination than the Philippines and a smaller one, which is exactly why it suits some students better. Class sizes are small, the cost is lower, and the teaching is in English.

why.title: Lower cost, without cutting the degree short
why.text: Tuition and living costs in Dili sit below most study-abroad medical routes, while the programme length, structure and NMC alignment stay the same. For many families this is the difference between possible and not.

why.title: Small cohorts, more contact
why.text: These are smaller universities than the Philippine campuses. That means less competition for time with teaching staff and for hands-on opportunities during rotations.

why.title: Taught in English
why.text: Teaching, assessment and clinical instruction are conducted in English, so there is no additional language qualification standing between you and the start of the course.

why.title: Both campuses in the capital
why.text: Both partner universities are in Dili, so accommodation, hospitals and the LIMRA support contact are all within the same city rather than spread across the country.

why.title: The honest version of the trade-off
why.text: Timor-Leste has a smaller Indian student community than the Philippines and fewer alumni to lean on. We would rather you hear that from us on the call than discover it after you land.

clinical.intro: Students at both Dili universities train in the country's main referral and regional hospitals, with supervised patient contact through the clinical years and an internship before graduation.
